brackets.section: 2026 Tax Rate Schedules for Full-Year Residents, Schedules A and B
brackets.note: Head of household uses Schedule A, the same schedule as single. The printed gross tax for the top bracket ($17,030.62 single, $22,707.70 joint) is reproduced by these brackets. Tax Foundation and PolicyEngine agree.

earnedIncomeCredit.note: A share of the federal credit by number of qualifying children: "one qualifying child ... 4 percent", two "11 percent", "3 or more ... 34 percent", and nothing without a child. Refundable. Full-year residents only. Wisconsin recomputes the federal credit under its own version of the tax code when its income adjustments apply, which is not modeled.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: Wisconsin earned income credit

standardDeduction.note: These are the maximum amounts, which only apply at low income. Sliding-scale rule from the 2026 Standard Deduction schedules, read against Wisconsin income. Single: $13,960 less 12% of income over $20,120, zero above $136,453. Joint: $25,840 less 19.778% of income over $29,040, zero above $159,690. Head of household: $18,030 less 22.515% of income over $20,120 for income up to $58,827, then the single formula ($13,960 less 12% of income over $20,120), zero above $136,453. The phaseOut points are the corners of those formulas at whole-dollar incomes: the start, the formula's value at the last dollar of each range, and zero one dollar later. For head of household the two formulas differ by a few cents at $58,827, hence the two adjacent points there. The Form 1 return itself uses a printed lookup table built from the same formulas, so a filed return can differ by a few dollars. Tax Foundation shows the same single and joint maximums and the same phase-out ends.

personalExemption.section: 2026 Estimated Income Tax Worksheet, line 2 footnote
personalExemption.note: $700 each for the filer, spouse and each dependent. Not indexed. Tax Foundation agrees.

rules.note: No local income taxes per Tax Foundation footnote (a), which does not list Wisconsin. Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions. No employee payroll contribution: the US Department of Labor's comparison lists worker unemployment contributions only in Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and disability insurance only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, and no paid leave or similar program with an employee contribution was found for this state on 2026-11-12.
notes: Wisconsin's standard deduction shrinks as income rises and is gone above $136,453 single or head of household and $159,690 joint. This is included.
Not modeled: the married couple credit for joint filers where both spouses work, 3% of the lower earner's income up to $480.
Not modeled: an extra $250 exemption for each filer who is 65 or older.
Not modeled: the itemized deduction credit and the homestead credit.
